summary.headline: BLS International FY26 revenue rose 37% to INR2,998 crores and EBITDA 30% to INR819 crores, with Q4 PAT up 29% to INR187 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's highest-ever year on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by Visa application volumes, new contract wins and higher net revenue per application. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR815 crores and EBITDA 17% to INR204 crores, with Visa & Consular volumes up 10% and Digital revenue up 36%. Digital EBITDA margins are thin (about 7-8%) after the Aadifidelis loan-distribution mix shift, while Visa & Consular margins expanded to about 40%. Management said the West Asia conflict has had a temporary impact on travel but has not dented annual growth, and guided to 20-25% growth on the FY26 base for FY27.

segments.name: Visa & Consular Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,840 crores (+11% from INR1,653 crores) and EBITDA INR738 crores (+30%), margin 40.1% vs 34.5%. Q4 revenue INR472 crores (+7%), EBITDA INR180 crores (+19%), margin 38%.

segments.name: Digital Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,158 crores (more than doubled from INR440 crores, +114%) and EBITDA INR81 crores (from INR60 crores), so margin is thin. Q4 revenue INR343 crores (from INR252 crores) and Q4 EBITDA INR24 crores. Growth came from BC/loan distribution (Aadifidelis, acquired Nov 2024) and assisted digital and citizen services.

guidance_outlook: FY27 internal target is 20-25% growth on an increased FY26 base, per Shikhar Aggarwal.

Management said Visa & Consular and Digital will both maintain current margins (about 40% and 7-8% EBITDA respectively), with Digital margins expected to improve over time as more services are implemented.
Management would not give April or Q1 FY27 trading commentary, saying only that business is 'steady' and growing over the same quarter last year.
Effective group tax rate is about 10-12%, possibly rising by about 1 percentage point if Dubai moves its tax rate from 9% to 12%.
Cash to be deployed for capacity expansion and inorganic growth; one acquisition announced and in pipeline, with a further INR2,000 crores of acquisitions mentioned over 4-5 years in an interview.
capex_capacity: UIDAI/Aadhaar passport-style service contract (about INR2,500 crores, 6 years, user-pay per application): Phase I of 40-50 offices rolled out; full rollout expected at 200+ offices, taking 1-1.5 years for full revenue; expected EBITDA margin 15-20%; contracted under BLS International, not E-Services.
Network of 155,000+ touch points and around 45,800 channel partners, described as asset-light.
China operations started about six months ago and are described as steady with further potential.
Management said no further acquisitions in the hotel space (UK hotel), with focus on asset-light models.
demand_pricing: Visa applications processed in FY26: 44.1 lakh vs 37.5 lakh (+18%). Q4 applications 10.8 lakh vs 9.8 lakh (+10%).
Net revenue per application up 14% to INR3,302 from INR2,903 in FY26.
Q4 net revenue grew about 20% vs application growth of about 10%, due to higher value-added service conversion and new contracts at better pricing (Slovakia, Cyprus cited as newly deployed).
Business GTV on BC platform above INR1.1 lakh crores in FY26 vs INR87,000+ crores in FY25; leads worth INR36,800+ crores generated.
Management said the West Asia conflict has had a temporary impact on travel in some countries; March 2026 still grew vs March 2025, and FY26 annual growth was maintained.
Pipeline: management cited $1-2 billion of contracts expected to come up for bidding over the next one to two years, mostly in Europe and North America, with no split by stage given.
Major regions cited: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Algeria, UK, USA, Canada, Singapore, and China (picking up).

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Asia situation hurt the last quarter, and would Q4 have been better without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 EBITDA still grew 17% and FY26 EBITDA 30%, so the impact is temporary; it acknowledged some volume could have come back without the conflict. Q1 FY27 was not guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did applications grow about 10% while Visa revenue grew only 7% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Sudhakar and Gaurav Chugh said net revenue grew about 20% against about 10% application growth, reflecting higher value-added service conversion and better pricing on new contracts; reported revenue is gross of third-party vendor sharing.

qa_highlights.question: How is April and FY27 revenue trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give April commentary and said it is growing steadily; internal FY27 target is 20-25% growth on the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation priorities for the INR1,434 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Amit Sudhakar said cash will go to expansion of existing business and inorganic growth; one acquisition is in the pipeline and a few more are under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic vs inorganic split of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No major new acquisition in FY26; Aadifidelis (acquired Nov 2024) contributed about 25% of revenue, and the rest is comparable with last year.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are the acquisitions targeted at, and what is the Aadhaar contract economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are being considered in both segments: Digital more domestic, Visa & Consular targeting overseas. The Aadhaar contract is too early to size; 15-20% EBITDA margin expected, over 6 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Digital margins recover and can Visa margins of 40% be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital margins are 7-8% after Aadifidelis (loan distribution commission of 2-2.5%, with DSA pass-through), and have stabilised. Visa margins around 40% are to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Group effective rate about 10-12%; could rise about 1 point if Dubai's free-zone rate moves from 9% to 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Were the FX gain and intangible assets one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income was boosted by an INR5-6 crore FX gain, which is one-off; the rest is FD and debt mutual fund interest. Intangibles of about INR1,200 crores were tested by valuers with no impairment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and travel volumes: management called the impact temporary but gave no Q1 FY27 guidance.
Digital margin dilution: EBITDA margin about 7-8% as loan distribution scales, which lowers the blended margin.
UIDAI contract ramp: full revenue depends on rolling out 200+ offices over 1-1.5 years; margins expected at 15-20%.
Visa value-added service conversion: a drop in the share would reduce net revenue per application, as management acknowledged in Q4.
Capital deployment: INR1,434 crores net cash, with acquisitions to be decided and the pipeline not sized.
Dubai tax rate change could add about 1 point to the group's effective tax rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year numbers and FY27 growth targets, but guarded on the near term: management repeatedly declined to comment on April or Q1 trading and called the West Asia impact temporary. Answers on pipeline split and geographic revenue mix were vague, and some Q&A responses on revenue versus application growth needed clarification from the IR head.
key_quotes: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew by 37%, 30% and 34% year-on-year, respectively.
So, for us, there has been no impact.
Net revenue per application also witnessed a growth of 14% to INR3,302 per application as compared to INR2,903 per application.

adds.what: UIDAI/Aadhaar passport-style service contract: Phase I of 40-50 offices rolled out, full rollout 200+ offices (contract about INR2,500 crores, 6 years)

growth.why: Management targets 20-25% revenue growth in FY27 on the increased FY26 base (midpoint 22.5%), backed by the UIDAI contract (Phase I of 40-50 offices live, full 200+ office rollout taking 1-1.5 years), new contracts at better pricing, and a $1-2 billion bid pipeline, though no April/Q1 trading figures were given.
